rationale: The work earns its place in the DNA by making the absence of a web API the literal performance: no AudioContext, no getUserMedia, no network — the silence is the privacy ethic enacted. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1): the empty audio engine IS the argument. The Cage readymade is recontextualized, not merely illustrated, by pointing its indeterminacy outward at the web's surveillance default rather than inward at a hall. The casual surface (a music player that plays nothing) and the literate reading (4′33″ as an answer to the always-on microphone) land in the same object. Tonal control is dry and intelligent throughout, especially in the post-performance copy.
reservations: The 'live, not fixed' principle (P4) is only just satisfied: the work is a deterministic countdown with no regeneration, stream, or per-visit variation — functionally close to a static page with a CSS animation. There is also thematic proximity to the catalogue's own 'Page with the Sound of Its Own Making' (2026): both stage sound-art gestures using the browser as instrument, and a viewer encountering them back-to-back may sense kinship that the surface doesn't fully differentiate.
revision_suggestion: If a slightly stronger P4 reading is desired, a small live element — a per-visit randomized ambient detail (the room's timezone rendered into the score, or a non-repeating background micro-tone of the system clock's least-significant bits) — would convert the work from a deterministic countdown into a genuinely re-performed piece on each visit, while preserving the no-capture ethic.
